### Import CSV Files

Save this Quarto document and both CSV files together in the lecture folder. In the Files pane, browse to that folder and choose **More \> Set As Working Directory**. Browsing alone does not change R's working directory.

```{r}

# Check the path and confirm that both files return TRUE before importing.

getwd()
file.exists("customer_data.csv", "store_transactions.csv")
```

```{r}

customer_data <- read_csv("customer_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

### Data Frames

```{r}

# This code displays the data frame.

customer_data
```

```{r}

glimpse(customer_data)
```

### Filter Observations

```{r}

# This code displays only customers with a college degree.

filter(customer_data, college_degree == "Yes")
```

```{r}

# This code displays only customers outside of the West region.

filter(customer_data, region != "West")
```

### Slice Observations

```{r}

# This code displays only the first 5 customers in the data frame.


slice(customer_data, 1:5)
```

### Arrange Observations

```{r}

# This code displays the customers in order of birth year.

arrange(customer_data, birth_year)
```

```{r}

# This code arranges them from youngest to oldest.

arrange(customer_data, desc(birth_year))
```

### Select Variables

```{r}
# this code selects two variables, region and review text

select(customer_data, region, review_text)
```

```{r}

# This code selects all the columns from region to review_text.

select(customer_data, region:review_text)
```

### Mutate Variables

```{r}

# This code changes the income column to be in terms of 1000s of dollars.

mutate(customer_data, income = income / 1000)
```

```{r}

# The code above displays a changed result but does not change customer_data.
# Assign the result if you want to keep it.

customer_data_adjusted <- mutate(customer_data, income = income / 1000)
```

### Join Data Frames

```{r}

# This will read in the transaction data (again, ensure that you're in the right working directory)

store_transactions <- read_csv("store_transactions.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}

glimpse(store_transactions)
```

A **left join** keeps all rows in the "left" or first data frame that you list, and all columns from both data frames.

```{r}

left_join(customer_data, store_transactions, join_by(customer_id))
```

An **inner join** keeps rows that have matching IDs along with all columns from both data frames.

```{r}

inner_join(customer_data, store_transactions, join_by(customer_id))
```

### Consecutive Lines of Code

```{r}
# Try out the pipe operator!

customer_data |> 
  filter(credit == 850, state == "WY")
```

### Your Turn!

Here, `approx_age` is approximate age in 2026, not age at the time of purchase.

```{r}

# Add comments between each line to explain what this code is doing!

customer_data |> 
  left_join(store_transactions, join_by(customer_id)) |> 
  filter(region == "West") |>
  filter(feb_2005 == max(feb_2005)) |>
  mutate(approx_age = 2026 - birth_year) |>
  select(approx_age, feb_2005) |>
  arrange(desc(approx_age)) |>
  slice(1)
```
